interactions.label: In paracetamol overdose, N-acetylcysteine (NAC) prevents hepatotoxicity primaril

params.question: In paracetamol overdose, N-acetylcysteine (NAC) prevents hepatotoxicity primarily by:

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: CYP2E1 inhibition is not the mechanism of NAC. NAC works downstream of NAPQI formation — it restores hepatic glutathione that conjugates and detoxifies NAPQI.

answers.text: Replenishing hepatic glutathione to conjugate and detoxify NAPQI

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: In overdose, glutathione is depleted below 30% of normal, allowing the reactive metabolite NAPQI to accumulate and cause centrilobular hepatic necrosis. NAC replenishes glutathione, restoring the capacity to detoxify NAPQI — most effective within 8–10 hours.
NAC does not enhance renal excretion. Its protective effect is intrahepatic — replenishing glutathione to detoxify the reactive metabolite NAPQI.

answers.text: Directly binding and neutralising paracetamol in the gastrointestinal tract

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: NAC does not act by binding paracetamol in the gut. It works at the hepatic level by replenishing glutathione stores depleted during overdose metabolism.

overallFeedback.feedback: NAC works by replenishing hepatic glutathione stores. In overdose, conjugation pathways saturate, more paracetamol is shunted through CYP2E1 to form NAPQI, and glutathione depletion allows NAPQI to cause hepatic necrosis. NAC restores this defence.

Well done! NAC replenishes hepatic glutathione, enabling conjugation of the hepatotoxic metabolite NAPQI. This is why early administration (within 8–10 hours) is critical — before glutathione depletion becomes irreversible.

interactions.label: A 5-year-old child from an old housing settlement presents with irritability, ab

params.question: A 5-year-old child from an old housing settlement presents with irritability, abdominal colic, and microcytic anaemia with basophilic stippling on peripheral smear. Which additional finding would further confirm lead poisoning?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Mees' lines (transverse white bands on fingernails) are characteristic of arsenic poisoning, not lead.
Kayser-Fleischer rings are pathognomonic of Wilson's disease (copper deposition in Descemet's membrane), not lead poisoning.

answers.text: Blue-black line along the gingival margin (Burton's line)

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Burton's lines — blue-black deposits of lead sulfide along the gingival margin — are pathognomonic of lead poisoning, alongside basophilic stippling and the clinical triad of anaemia, colic, and neuropathy.
Alopecia and garlic-scented breath are features of arsenic poisoning. Lead poisoning produces anaemia with basophilic stippling, abdominal colic, and motor neuropathy (e.g. wrist drop in adults).

overallFeedback.feedback: Burton's lines (blue-black gingival lead sulfide deposits) are pathognomonic of lead poisoning. Mees' lines and garlic breath suggest arsenic; Kayser-Fleischer rings indicate copper overload (Wilson's disease).
Excellent! Burton's lines, basophilic stippling, lead colic, and wrist drop (in adults) form the classic clinical picture of chronic lead poisoning.

params.question: A 30-year-old man presents with pruritic papules in finger webspaces and his partner has similar lesions. Scabies is confirmed. Which treatment protocol is correct?

answers.text: Permethrin 5% cream from neck downward to all skin surfaces, washed off after 8–14 hours, repeated after one week

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Permethrin 5% cream is applied to ALL skin surfaces from neck down (including webspaces, genitalia, under fingernails) at night, washed off after 8–14 hours, and repeated after one week to kill newly hatched mites. All household members and sexual contacts must be treated simultaneously.

answers.text: Permethrin 5% cream applied to affected areas only, washed off after 1 hour

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Permethrin must be applied to ALL skin surfaces from neck down — not just visible lesions — because mites burrow beyond clinically apparent areas. Contact time is 8–14 hours, not 1 hour.

answers.text: Lindane 1% lotion applied to affected areas twice daily for 7 days

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Lindane is not first-line due to neurotoxicity risk (CNS toxicity, especially in children). Permethrin 5% cream, a synthetic pyrethroid, is the global first-line scabicide.

answers.text: Permethrin 1% cream from head to toe, left on for 24 hours

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Permethrin 5% (not 1%) is the therapeutic concentration for scabies; 1% is the pediculosis formulation. Application is from neck down (not head to toe), for 8–14 hours — not 24 hours.

overallFeedback.feedback: The correct protocol: permethrin 5% cream applied from neck down to ALL skin surfaces, left on for 8–14 hours, repeated after one week. All household members and sexual contacts must be treated simultaneously to prevent re-infestation.

Correct! Key elements of scabies management: permethrin 5% concentration, applied neck-downward to all skin surfaces, 8–14 hour contact time, repeat at one week, and simultaneous treatment of all contacts.

interactions.label: A 22-year-old contact lens wearer presents with a painful red eye, photophobia,

params.question: A 22-year-old contact lens wearer presents with a painful red eye, photophobia, and a corneal infiltrate. Which topical antibiotic is most appropriate as first-line therapy?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Chloramphenicol is cost-effective for routine bacterial conjunctivitis but lacks the broader gram-negative coverage required for contact-lens-associated bacterial keratitis.
Neosporin is appropriate for mild bacterial conjunctivitis but is not first-line for keratitis, where broader and more potent antimicrobial coverage is required.
Erythromycin has limited gram-negative coverage and is inadequate as monotherapy for bacterial keratitis, particularly in contact lens wearers where gram-negative organisms are common pathogens.

Fluoroquinolones (ciprofloxacin 0.3%, ofloxacin 0.3%) are first-line for bacterial keratitis and contact-lens-associated ocular infections because of their broad-spectrum activity including superior gram-negative coverage and excellent corneal penetration.

overallFeedback.feedback: Fluoroquinolones (ciprofloxacin 0.3%, ofloxacin 0.3%) are first-line for bacterial keratitis and contact-lens infections. Chloramphenicol and Neosporin are adequate for milder conjunctivitis but lack the coverage needed for keratitis.
Well done! Fluoroquinolones are first-line for bacterial keratitis and contact-lens-associated infections due to their broad gram-negative coverage and excellent corneal penetration.
